summary: A note from MIT-DMCG on Host 106 saying it now offers the Echo and Discard services from RFC 347 and 348 on sockets 7 and 9. It describes its choices: refusing a connection if the machine is too busy and aborting after two idle minutes. It asks whether a random character generator service would also be useful.

plainLanguage.summary: MIT-DMCG reported that Host 106 could respond to Echo and Discard requests. The note explains when connections would be refused or closed and asks whether users wanted a random-character service.

subtitle: MIT-DMCG announces two network test processes

tldr.problem: The note reports that Host 106 had installed Echo and Discard processes and explains their connection limits.
tldr.mechanism: The processes use sockets 7 and 9; the host refuses new connections when it cannot support another process and closes inactive connections.
tldr.outcome: The author asks whether the network would benefit from a separate random-character service.

today: RFC 361 announces Echo and Discard processes at Host 106 and asks about a possible third service. The text does not report a decision on the proposed random-character generator.

sections.title: Echo and Discard on Host 106
sections.content:
Bob Bressler reports that MIT-DMCG on Host 106 had daemon processes to respond to the Echo and Discard RFCs. The processes were available on sockets 7 and 9.

The note identifies the services by their related RFCs but does not assign one of the two socket numbers to each service.
sections.plainLanguage: Host 106 had processes for the Echo and Discard services. They were available on sockets 7 and 9.

sections.title: When a Connection Is Refused or Closed
sections.content: If the machine was too full to support another daemon process, it would refuse the offered connection by sending a CLS in response to the request. If no activity occurred for two consecutive minutes, the connection would be aborted. The note defines inactivity as no input characters arriving or output being blocked while waiting for allocation.
sections.plainLanguage: A full machine would refuse another connection. A connection with no activity for two minutes would be closed.

sections.title: Question About a Random Character Service
sections.content:
The author asks whether there was a need for a third service that generated random characters. He notes that many systems had terminal-testing programs that could provide this function and suggests that a network service might help test new NCPs and gather statistics.

This RFC asks for opinions; it does not announce that such a service had been implemented.
sections.plainLanguage: The author asks whether a service that sends random characters would be useful for testing. The notice does not say that this service was already available.
